transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well, I guess what finally brought me in is that I just don't feel like myself anymore. I used to always make time for things—painting, hiking, my choir, Sunday family gatherings. But now, even when I have a free hour, I just sit there. I just find myself unable to care about any of it.
How long have you been feeling this way—this lack of interest in things you used to enjoy?

Well, it's been building for about eight months now. I think it really started right around the time I took over the STEM-Arts curriculum initiative at the school. It just sort of... started then, and it hasn't gotten any better. So, yeah, about eight months.
Besides losing interest in things, how has your mood been over these eight months? Would you say you've been feeling sad, down, or depressed?

Yes, I would definitely say I've been feeling down. Um, most days it just feels like there's a heavy gray film over everything. I can be standing right there in a classroom full of students, or just at home with my husband, and I still feel completely hollow. I just find myself feeling close to tears a lot of the time.
Before these eight months, have you ever had a period in your life—lasting at least a couple of weeks—where you felt this same kind of persistent sadness and loss of interest in things?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days or stressful weeks before, like anyone else, but nothing like this. This is the first time I've felt this... empty for this long.
Over these past eight months, how has your sleep been? Have you noticed any changes—like difficulty falling asleep, waking up in the middle of the night, or sleeping more than usual?

My sleep has been all over the place for months, honestly. Um, I definitely have a hard time falling asleep because I just lie awake replaying grant details in my head. And then I usually wake up around three or four in the morning. But even on the days when I do manage to sleep a little longer, I just... I get up feeling like I never rested at all.
Over these past eight months, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight?
No, not really. Um, my appetite has been pretty much the same as always. I haven't gained or lost any weight that I've noticed. I still eat my regular meals, so... no changes there.

Over these past eight months, have people around you noticed any changes in how fast or slow you move or speak? For example, do you find yourself moving more slowly, or do others say you seem sluggish—or conversely, do you feel more restless or fidgety than usual?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. And no one has said anything to me about it, either. I don't feel like I'm moving any slower than usual, and I'm not really restless or fidgety. So, no, I don't think there have been any changes there.
Over these past eight months, have you been feeling worthless or guilty about things? Or do you find yourself blaming yourself for problems?

Yeah, I do. Um, especially at work. Whenever anything goes wrong with the curriculum project I'm involved in—even if it's just something really small—I immediately blame myself. I just keep thinking that I'm letting the students down. And then I start feeling guilty, like... like I'm wasting all the sacrifices my parents made for me to even have this kind of opportunity in the first place. So, yes, I've been feeling a lot of guilt about things like that.
Over these past eight months, have you had any thoughts about harming yourself, or any thoughts about death or suicide?

Well, um... yeah, I have. Sometimes, especially on late nights when I'm working in the studio, I just catch myself thinking that... that it would be a relief if I just didn't wake up. I haven't actually made a plan or anything like that, but... just having those thoughts really scares me. It scared me enough that I actually told my husband recently that I couldn't keep handling them on my own. So, yes, those thoughts have been there.

Have you ever had a period—even just a few days—where you felt unusually energetic, optimistic, or 'up,' where you needed much less sleep than normal but still felt rested, or where you were unusually productive or took on a lot of projects at once?

No, I haven't. I've never really felt like that. I mean, I have times where I might get a little bit of work done, but nothing where I feel unusually energetic or like I don't need sleep. If anything, I'm just tired. So no, I haven't had any periods like what you're describing.
